gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant reserve strengthening of GBP 41.070 million (28.48% of opening gross reserves) for prior underwriting years in 2021. This adverse development was primarily driven by large catastrophe losses from the 2020 underwriting year, including winter storm Uri and hurricane Ida, which largely fell below reinsurance attachment points. Additionally, there was an GBP 8.2 million increase in COVID-19 loss reserves, mainly impacting the property reinsurance account. Other prior year events contributing to the strengthening included the Iowa derecho.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2021 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 144.225m. During calendar 2021 there was adverse prior-year development totalling GBP 16.073m (a strengthening of reserves, c.11.15% of opening gross claims) largely driven by property-related catastrophe and large loss events and pandemic-related exposures. The managing agent identifies key contributors as winter storm Uri, hurricane Ida, covid losses and the Iowa derecho, with much of the deterioration arising on the 2020 and prior underwriting years, particularly within property reinsurance exposures.
raw_causal_phrases: the key drivers of these losses in the year, included winter storm Uri (GBP 12.9 million), hurricane Ida (GBP 1.8 million), Measat (GBP 0.4 million) and adverse development on 2020 losses, including covid losses (GBP 8.2 million) and the Iowa derecho (GBP 2.3 million).
The booked reserves for these losses at 31 December 2021 are GBP 19.1 million (2020: GBP 10.9 million) gross of reinsurance and GBP 19.1 million (2020: GBP 9.8 million) net of reinsurance.

The 2021 result for the 2020 and prior underwriting years was materially impacted by several large and catastrophe losses in the year, which were largely under the attachment points of the outwards reinsurance protections, notably losses arising from winter storm Uri and hurricane Ida.
